competition: Malaysia IMO National Selection Test 2 (IMONST 2) — Senior

problems.problem: Given a trapezium with two parallel sides of integer lengths $m$ and $n$, prove that it can be divided into congruent triangles. Two triangles are congruent when they have the same shape and size.
Prove that $$1-\frac12+\frac13-\frac14+\cdots+\frac1{2019}-\frac1{2020}=\frac1{1001}+\frac1{1002}+\cdots+\frac1{2020}.$$
Find all integers $n$ such that $12n^2+12n+11$ is a four-digit number whose four digits are equal.

Four circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2,\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4$ have the following external tangencies: $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ at $A$, $\Gamma_2$ and $\Gamma_3$ at $B$, $\Gamma_3$ and $\Gamma_4$ at $C$, and $\Gamma_4$ and $\Gamma_1$ at $D$. Prove that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is cyclic.
Let $p,q$ be real numbers such that $x^2+px+q=0$ has two distinct real roots $x_1,x_2$. Suppose $|x_1-x_2|=1$ and $|p-q|=1$. Prove that $p,q,x_1,x_2$ are all integers.

In a one-player game, a player starts with score $0$ and the number $20$ on an empty whiteboard. At each step she erases one integer $a$ and writes two positive integers $b,c$ with $b+c=a$, adding $bc$ to her score. She repeats this until only $1$s remain, when the game ends.
For example, replacing $20$ with $14,6$ gives score $84$. Then replacing $14$ with $9,5$ adds $45$, giving score $129$. Next she may replace any of $5,6,9$, and continues until the game ends.
Alya and Bob play separately. Alya obtains the highest possible final score and Bob the lowest. What is the difference between their final scores?
Find all values of $n$ for which a rectangle with integer side lengths has perimeter $n$ and area $2n$.

Six teams participate in a hockey tournament. Each team plays every other team once. A win earns $3$ points, a draw $1$ and a loss $0$. After the tournament the teams are ranked by total points, with no ties. Each team except the bottom team has $2$ points more than the team immediately below it. Prove that the fourth-place team won two games and lost three.

Let $x,y$ be rational numbers satisfying $$x^5+y^5=2x^2y^2.$$
Prove that $\sqrt{1-xy}$ is rational. A rational number is a number of the form $a/b$ with integers $a,b$ and $b\ne0$.
An octagon has all its interior angles equal and all its side lengths integers. Prove that every pair of opposite sides has equal lengths.

There are $n$ guests at a gathering. Any two are either friends or not friends. Every guest is friends with exactly four others. Whenever a guest is not friends with two other guests, those two cannot be friends with each other. Determine all possible values of $n$.
Prove that there is a positive integer $m$ such that the decimal representation of $5^{2021}m$ has no even digits.
A circle $\Gamma$ has center $I$, and every side of triangle $ABC$ is tangent to $\Gamma$. A line $\ell$ bisects both the area and perimeter of $ABC$. Prove that $\ell$ passes through $I$.

There are $n$ integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfying $$a_1+\cdots+a_n=0,\qquad a_1a_2\cdots a_n=n.$$
Determine all possible values of $n$.
Prove that there is a multiple of $2^{2022}$ with $2022$ digits, all of which are $1$ or $2$.
A pentagon $ABCDE$ has all its interior angles less than $180^\circ$. Prove that if $\angle ABC=\angle ADE$ and $\angle ADB=\angle AEC$, then $\angle BAC=\angle DAE$.
Let $a,b,r,s$ be positive integers with $a\ge2$ and with $a,b$ having no common prime factor. Prove that if $a^r+b^r$ is divisible by $a^s+b^s$, then $r$ is divisible by $s$.

A football league has $n$ teams. Each team plays every other team once. A win earns $2$ points, a tie $1$ and a loss $0$. After the league, for every nonempty subset $S$ of the teams, there is a team, which may or may not belong to $S$, whose total points from games against teams in $S$ is odd. Prove that $n$ is even.
Prove that infinitely many positive integers can be expressed both as the sum of $2001$ distinct perfect squares and as the sum of $2023$ distinct positive perfect cubes.
Prove that if $x,y,n$ are positive integers satisfying $$x^{2024}+y^{2024}=2^n,$$ then $x=y$.

Fix an integer $n\ge1$. What is the smallest $m$ for which $n$ queens can be placed on an $m\times n$ chessboard without two attacking each other? A queen attacks horizontally, vertically or diagonally over any distance.

A right triangle $ABC$ has $\angle BAC=90^\circ$. Points $D,E,F$ lie on $BC,CA,AB$, respectively, with $AD\perp BC$ and $EF\parallel BC$. Point $G$ lies on $AC$ with $AG=CE$. Prove that $\angle GDF=90^\circ$.
Find the smallest positive $m$ such that whenever $a,b,c$ are the side lengths of a triangle and $a^2+b^2>mc^2$, then $c$ must be the shortest side length.
Ivan has a parallelogram with interior angles $60^\circ,120^\circ,60^\circ,120^\circ$ and integer side lengths. Can one of its diagonals have length $\sqrt{2024}$?
Suppose $a,b,c,d$ are positive real numbers with $a\ge b\ge c\ge d$ and $ab^2c^3d^4=1$. Help Janson prove that $a+b+c+d\ge4$.

A sequence of integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ is called good if $a_1=1$ and $a_{i+1}-a_i$ is $1$ or $2$ for every $i\ge1$. Find all positive integers $n$ that cannot be written as $n=a_1+\cdots+a_k$, where $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ form a good sequence.

Ivan claims that for every positive integer $n$,
$$\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{n}{1^3}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{n}{2^3}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{n}{3^3}}\right\rfloor+\cdots=\left\lfloor\sqrt[3]{\frac{n}{1^2}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\sqrt[3]{\frac{n}{2^2}}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\sqrt[3]{\frac{n}{3^2}}\right\rfloor+\cdots.$$
Why is he correct? Here $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the floor function.
For every $n\ge1$, let $a_n$ be the fraction $k/2^n$ closest to $1/3$ among all integer values of $k$. Prove that $2a_{i+2}=a_{i+1}+a_i$ for every $i\ge1$.

Janson finds $2025$ dogs on a circle. He wants to choose some, possibly none, such that no two chosen dogs have exactly two dogs, chosen or not, between them. Let $S_1$ count these choices.
Ivan finds $2025$ cats on a circle. He wants to choose some, possibly none, such that no two chosen cats have exactly five cats, chosen or not, between them. Let $S_2$ count these choices.
(a) Prove that $S_1=S_2$. (b) Prove that both are perfect cubes.

Rui Xuen has a circle $\omega$ with center $O$ and an inscribed square $ABCJ$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$, and $\Gamma$ the circle through $J,O,M$. Circle $\Gamma$ meets line $AJ$ again at $P\ne J$ and $\omega$ again at $Q\ne J$. Point $R$ lies on $BC$ with $RC=3RB$. Help Rui Xuen prove that $P,Q,R$ are collinear.

An elephant is at number $0$ and can move forward $k$ steps or backward $1$ step. Determine the smallest $m$ for which there is a choice of $k$ such that, for every $a\le2025$, the elephant can reach number $a$ in at most $m$ moves.

Let $ABC$ have circumcenter $O$ and orthocenter $H$. Line $AO$ meets the circumcircle of $BHC$ at $X,Y$. Prove that if $\angle AOH=90^\circ$, then the midpoint of $XY$ lies on the circumcircle of $ABC$.

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Determine, in terms of $n$, the maximum of
$$x_1(x_2-x_1)+x_2(x_3-x_2)+\cdots+x_{n-1}(x_n-x_{n-1})$$
over positive real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with $x_1\le x_2\le\cdots\le x_n\le n$.

A tile is a collection of orthogonally connected unit squares. Is there a set $S$ of five pairwise distinct tiles such that all contain the same number of squares, none is a rectangle, and an $m\times n$ board can be tiled using tiles from $S$ if and only if $2025$ divides both $m$ and $n$? Rotation is allowed, reflection is forbidden, and not all tile types need be used.
Let $ABC$ be acute with circumcenter $O$. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $BC,AO$, respectively. The tangent to the circumcircle at $A$ meets line $BC$ at $D$. If $DM=DN$, find $\angle A$.

Let $S$ be a set of $2025$ distinct integers. A subset $T\subseteq S$ is progression-free if it contains no three elements in arithmetic progression. Prove that $S$ has a progression-free subset of size at least (i) $37$, and (ii) $119$.
